reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's rendered text and re-read and approved the corrected text.

Blockers fixed before approval: the frame now correctly has the owl counsellor Hook-Nose telling the tale to the owl king Foe-Crusher; the club is consistently a stick (ದೊಣ್ಣೆ) that the man only holds and never raises; the man's caste is dropped with disclosure.
The ghost and the thief are comic, the thief runs off unhurt, and the closing line about each rogue giving away the other is disclosed as added; no em dashes.
2026-10-05: the coordinator changed only the age label from 8–12 to 8+ under the new age bands (2+, 8+, 10+, 12+, 16+); no story text changed, so the text approval above still applies.
illustrations: Six equal 512px panels; seams measured exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024 on the published WebP; 1024x1536, under 650 KB; no gutters, dividing lines, bleed or vignettes; no text in any panel.

Final sheet is a composite of one generation and two edit passes. The first corrected the ghost's smile in panel 2 and turned the panel 5 raised palm into a palm-up prayer hand; the second removed a third cow behind the man in panel 1 and the tooth flecks on the ghost in panels 2 to 4.

Panel 1: the smiling poor man (grey stubble, white dhoti, striped shawl, no caste markers) feeds hay to exactly two brown-and-white cows by his thatched hut; the same two cows appear in panels 3 and 6.

Panels 2 to 4: the thief (same brown complexion as the villager, generic storybook costume) and a round, legless, misty ghost walk, then argue and point at each other at the door while the man appears with an oil lamp.

Panel 5: the man prays with eyes closed, one palm up, the stick lowered with its tip on the ground; the ghost dissolves and the thief runs off unhurt with an empty sack. Panel 6: the man rests between his sleeping cows under the moon.
Accepted minor issues: the ghost looks blissful rather than frightened as it melts in panel 5, and a tiny pale highlight inside the ghost's mouth in panel 3 is visible only at high zoom.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age suitability has not been tested with children.
Source fidelity was checked against the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; not every scene was checked in the app in dark mode.
